summary: Hartmut-Ortwin Feistel was an Indologist who studied under Paul Thieme. He held posts at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 1989, 2008) and the Oriental Department of the Royal Library of Berlin (attested 1982, 1992–1994).

Haruhiko Masaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Gakushuin University and the University of Tokyo. He served as a professor at Nagasaki University from around 1975 to 2004.
Haruka Yanagisawa (1944–2015) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He held academic posts at Chiba University (~1985–1994) and the University of Tokyo (~1994–2005).

Harumi Hirano Ziegler is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She completed her MA in 1994 and her PhD in 2001 at the University of California, Los Angeles, where she studied under doctoral supervisor Robert E. Buswell Jr.

Harunaga Isaacson is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology scholar who studied at Groningen and Leiden under Hans T. Bakker and Tilmann Vetter. He held posts at Oxford, the University of Pennsylvania, and the University of Hamburg.

Harushige Kōzu (1908–1973) was a linguist who studied under Naoshiro Tsuji at the University of Tokyo and attended Balliol College, Oxford. He served as assistant, lecturer, and associate professor at Tokyo before becoming professor at Musashi University in 1968.

Harvey B. Aronson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed doctoral work under Richard Hugh Robinson. He served as a professor at the University of Virginia (attested 1988) and co-directed the Dawn Mountain Center for Tibetan Buddhism.

Harvey Paul Alper (1945–1987) was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Pennsylvania (~1970–1976) and served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Southern Methodist University from 1974 to 1987.

Hasmukh Dhirajlal Sankalia (1908–1989) was an archaeologist, historian, and Indologist. He studied under Henry Heras and later under F. J. Richards at University College London, and served as a professor at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (1945–1946).

Haya Akegarasu (1877–1954) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure who studied under Manshi Kiyozawa and attended Otani University. He later served as head of administration at Higashi Hongan-ji (~1951–1954) and as chief administrator of Shinshu Otani-ha.
Heather Stoddard is a Tibetologist and historian who studied at SOAS University of London and under D. C. Lau, Samten Gyaltsen Karmay, and Nicole Vandier-Nicolas (~1975–1983).

Heeraman Tiwari is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who earned his D.Phil. at Oxford under Bimal Krishna Matilal and Richard Gombrich. He has held positions at Jawaharlal Nehru University, Heidelberg University, and the Hebrew University of Jerusalem.
Hege Myrlund Larsen is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who completed a PhD at the University of Bergen under the supervision of Bruce Kapferer (attested 2009).
Hegoda Khemananda is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who served as Vice Principal of Vidyodaya Pirivena and Director of Dharma Paryeshanalaya (both attested 1993).

Heidi Fjeld is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who completed her doctorate under Signe Howell at the University of Oslo, with studies at Oxford. She later served as a postdoctoral fellow at the University of Oslo (~2006–2009).

Heidi I. Koppl is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her MA at the University of Copenhagen under the supervision of Christian K. Wedemeyer and studied under traditional teacher Sherab Zangpo.

Heidi R. M. Pauwels is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned her PhD at the University of Washington under Alan Entwistle. She lectured at SOAS (1994–1996) before becoming a professor at the University of Washington.

Heike Oberlin is an Indologist who studied at the University of Tübingen, Kerala Kalamandalam, and the University of Würzburg. She held positions at Tübingen (2005–2008), Kerala Kalamandalam (2018), and Sapienza University of Rome (2025).

Heimo Rau (1912–1993) was an Indologist and historian who earned his PhD from the University of Vienna. He worked at Staatliche Museen zu Berlin, directed Goethe-Institut branches, and taught Indian art and archaeology at Heidelberg University (1968–1982).

Hein Htet Kyaw is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Edinburgh Napier, James Cook, and Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya universities. In 2024, he served as Director of Australasia for Atheist Alliance International.
